synthesis: Read the JACS sulfa-drug paper on the CSP overprediction problem: it tackles why ranked landscapes list far more polymorphs than experiment finds, a core issue for your DFT-ranked GA searches. The AlphaTensor landmark (2022) shows RL-guided search discovering new matrix-multiplication algorithms.

landmark.title: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning
landmark.abstract: Abstract Improving the efficiency of algorithms for fundamental computations can have a widespread impact, as it can affect the overall speed of a large amount of computations. Matrix multiplication is one such primitive task, occurring in many systems—from neural networks to scientific computing routines. The automatic discovery of algorithms using machine learning offers the prospect of reaching beyond human intuition and outperforming the current best human-designed algorithms. However, automating the algorithm discovery procedure is intricate, as the space of possible algorithms is enormou
landmark.seed_title: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning
landmark.worth_30_min: AlphaTensor recast algorithm discovery as a single-player game (TensorGame) and used AlphaZero-style learned search to find matrix multiplication decompositions, improving on human-derived results that had stood since Strassen for some sizes. It showed that learned policy and value networks plus MCTS can navigate enormous discrete combinatorial spaces and produce verifiable new mathematics. This is the AlphaGo-search tier that the reader explicitly wants.
landmark.inspiration: Treat polymorph search as a sequential game. A learned policy could propose cell, space-group or molecular-placement moves, and a value net could estimate the lattice energy reachable from a partial structure. This could replace or guide GA mutation and crossover in GAtor. Also consider synthetic-demonstration pretraining (random decompositions to train the policy) as a parallel to generating synthetic packings, and symmetry-aware data augmentation.
landmark.foundations: AlphaZero: MCTS guided by policy and value networks, trained by self-play. Also covered: tensor-rank decomposition as a formulation of bilinear algorithm cost, and designing reward and action spaces for huge discrete search. The paper uses symmetry and change-of-basis augmentation, and mixes synthetic demonstrations with RL. Finally, contrast learned search against evolutionary and global optimizers like basin-hopping.
landmark.reading_guide: Start with Fig. 1 (the tensor game formulation), then Fig. 2 (network architecture and training). Read Fig. 3 for which matrix sizes improved. Skim the hardware-specific speedup results. In Methods, focus on action-space sampling, synthetic demonstrations and augmentation. Skip the detailed transformer architecture and the modular-arithmetic specifics. Spend the last 5 minutes mapping the game onto CSP.

items.title: The Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa Drugs
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.abstract: Abstract Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computation

rubric.why: Central MCSP problem (overprediction) tackled by the Price group with experimental validation of predicted forms; directly relevant to the reader's ranking and landscape work.

items.summary: Quantifies CSP overprediction for sulfadiazine/sulfamerazine using finite-temperature MD clustering (~60% reduction), DFT+D/phonon reranking, and CSP-guided experiments yielding new solid-solution and templated polymorphs.

items.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
items.abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. We make two technical contributions on top of DTS that are particularly relevant for AI-for-science applications. First, we show how to use existing property-conditional generative models (e.g., models fine-tuned for classifier-free guidance) as guided proposals inside DTS, without distorting the target distribution. Second, we extend DTS to multi-objective sampling, so that a single search produces samples spanning an entire Pareto front. items.title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
items.abstract: Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. However, generalist LLMs do not effectively handle large sets of 3D coordinates, whereas specialist generative models of 3D molecules cannot reach the controllability afforded by language. To bridge these capabilities, we propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model for any sequence of text and 3D molecules. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to the clean tokens before it, without increasing context size. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolvation to molecular conformer search to adsorption on metal surfaces, with associated evaluation metrics and baselines. items.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
items.abstract: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. items.title: Solving Molecular Crystal Structures through Experimental PXRD-Guided Sequential Crystal Structure Prediction
items.abstract: Structure determination of organic molecular crystals relies heavily on single-crystal X-ray diffraction, yet suitable single crystals are often difficult to obtain. A common alternative uses crystal structure prediction (CSP) to generate candidate structures for subsequent comparison with experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) patterns. Such trial-and-error searches across multiple space groups incur substantial computational costs. Here, we introduce a structure determination protocol that uses experimental PXRD together with molecular structure as inputs to guide CSP from the outset. A multimodal neural network predicts probabilities for candidate space groups, which are then searched sequentially in descending probability order. Candidate structures are evaluated using PXRD agreement and relative energies, and the search terminates when a candidate satisfies the matching criterion. In a retrospective evaluation of 11 molecular-crystal systems, the protocol returned candidate sets containing structures matching the experimental crystal packing in nine cases. rubric.why: Directly MCSP-relevant and practical PXRD-guided pruning, but modest validation (9/11 systems) and an efficiency gain rather than new search or ranking SOTA.

items.summary: Multimodal network predicts space-group probabilities from experimental PXRD plus molecular graph; CSP then searches space groups sequentially by probability, terminating on PXRD/energy match, cutting cost versus 22-group exhaustive search.

items.title: Constrained Crystal Structure Prediction
items.abstract: Abstract The aim of first-principles crystal structure prediction (CSP) is computational identification of a compound’s experimentally isolable polymorph(s). The structure generation stage of CSP typically leads to hundreds of thousands of candidate structures across multiple space groups. However, in many use cases, experimental powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) data is available from high-throughput polymorph screening studies, but the crystal structure is not yet solved. For such cases, we propose using indexed lattice parameters to constrain the CSP search space. Searching only specific unit-cell dimensions allows a large reduction in the number of structures generated, whilst adding confidence that the experimental structure is retained in the search pool when advancing to density-functional reranking of the most likely candidates. Examples are shown for the cases of several small organic molecules, specifically uracil, paracetamol, progesterone, and four forms of the prolific polymorph-former, ROY. rubric.why: Directly MCSP and practically useful, but the idea of PXRD-constrained search is fairly incremental; success hinges on force-field quality, and the tests are small-scale.

items.summary: Uses indexed PXRD lattice parameters to constrain CSP structure generation to fixed unit cells, then DFT reranks; tested on uracil, paracetamol, progesterone and four ROY forms.

items.title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
items.abstract: We present a computational framework that combines machine-learning-based discovery with rigorous computer-assisted numerical certification and formal verification for strongly nonlinear partial differential equations. We demonstrate the approach for periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves. Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism, with the wave profile, wave speed and, in continuation experiments, surface tension learned directly from the governing equations without training data. Through a staged training and refinement procedure, the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. A single formulation recovers high-amplitude Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples. Continuation from a high-amplitude Wilton ripple in surface tension reveals new high-amplitude candidate solutions. We freeze one candidate as an explicit finite representation and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic, accounting for floating-point roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors. items.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
items.abstract: Abstract The accurate quantum chemical calculation of excited states is a challenging task, often requiring computationally demanding methods. When entire ground and excited potential energy surfaces (PESs) are desired, for instance, to predict the interaction of light excitation and structural changes, one is often forced to use cheaper computational methods at the cost of reduced accuracy. Here we introduce a method for the geometrically transferable optimization of neural network wavefunctions that leverages weight sharing and a dynamical ordering of electronic states. Our method enables the efficient prediction of ground- and excited-state PESs and their intersections at the highest accuracy, demonstrating up to two orders of magnitude cost reduction compared with single-point calculations. We validate our approach on four challenging excited-state PESs, namely, ethylene, the carbon dimer, the methylenimmonium cation and a rubredoxin active site model containing 96 electrons, illustrating the potential of transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo as a practical framework for studying electronic excitations in molecules.

rubric.why: Solid Noe-group advance in deep QMC excited states, but incremental within the neural-wavefunction line and far from MCSP needs; not landmark tier.

items.summary: Transferable neural-network wavefunction (deep QMC) optimization across geometries for excited states, via weight sharing and dynamic state ordering; claims ~100x cost reduction vs single-point runs, including conical intersections.

items.title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
items.abstract: The electronic Schrödinger equation encodes a molecule's electronic structure and quantum properties, but solving it scales exponentially with the number of electrons. Solving this equation with neural-network variational Monte Carlo (VMC) has reached chemical accuracy on the ground state of small molecules; extending this success to excited states is constrained by two existing paradigms. Penalty-based methods need $K$ Laplacians per step but require tuning the overlap-penalty weights against the energy gaps they aim to compute. Natural excited states VMC (NES-VMC) is penalty-free, but it combines the $K$ ansatzes into one determinant, whose local energy requires $K^2$ Laplacians per step. We resolve this trade-off via low-rank approximation (LoRA) reparameterization of the rank-$K$ variational objective. The reparameterized objective admits a VMC-compatible stochastic gradient estimator via MCMC sampling from the per-state Born densities, and a sequential nesting scheme recovers the lowest $K$ eigenstates in eigenvalue order.
